newsitem.title: USA: American Greetings to overhaul top card line.
newsitem.headline: American Greetings to overhaul top card line.

text.p: American Greetings Corp., the No. 2 greeting card seller in the United States, announced an overhaul Thursday to its largest greeting card line in an attempt to reflect changing demographics.

The "All New American Way" marketing strategy will replace 80 percent of the birthday and everyday cards offered by the company, putting more than 100 million new cards in store shelves over 16 months beginning in July.
The new cards will reflect multi-culturalism, changing attitudes toward ageing and changing family dynamics, the company told a news conference.
For example, American Greetings will introduce smaller note-sized cards that can be slipped into a child's lunch box.
In addition to traditional "Get Well" cards, it will make cards that express words of encouragement to someone with a long-term illness.
New multi-cultural versing in everyday cards, with phrases such as "You go, Girl!" and "Muchas Gracias" will also be included, the company said.
The company said the new marketing strategy is based on changing lifestyle and demographic trends that are signalling new consumer communications needs.

"These emerging trends are changing consumer attitudes and will drive purchasing decisions going forward," said American Greetings president Edward Fruchtenbaum. "This is a magnitude of change in greeting cards seen only once each generation."
The company said costs of the overhaul are embedded in current projections and it does not expect the overhaul to affect earnings.

Everyday and birthday card sales accounted for 44 percent of American Greetings' $2.16 billion sales in 1996, compared with 22 percent for holiday cards, which will not be affected by the change, the company said.

The company said it is developing a marketing and advertising plan for the strategy, but did not release details about the campaign. The marketing plan will not be launched until the middle of 1998, when the roll-out to the 30,000 retailers that carry American Greeting's products gets under way.
